claims.text: In complementary base pairing a purine pairs with a pyrimidine: adenine pairs with thymine (with uracil in RNA) through two hydrogen bonds, and cytosine pairs with guanine through three hydrogen bonds. Because every pair holds one purine and one pyrimidine, each pair has the same width along the helix.

claims.text: Base pairing matters because the base sequence of one strand fixes the base sequence of the other, so each strand can act as a template for an accurate copy of the molecule. Hydrogen bonds are weak singly, so the strands can be separated when the DNA is copied, but together they hold the helix stable. A region rich in cytosine and guanine tends to separate less easily than a region of equal length rich in adenine and thymine, because it has more hydrogen bonds per base pair.

claims.text: DNA is replicated during S phase of interphase, before mitosis. The double helix is unwound and the hydrogen bonds between base pairs are broken, so each old strand is exposed as a template. Free nucleotides pair with the exposed bases by complementary base pairing, and neighbouring nucleotides are joined to form a new strand against each old strand. Replication begins at many places along a eukaryotic chromosome. Afterwards each chromosome consists of two sister chromatids, each holding one of the two new DNA molecules.

claims.text: Two enzymes do most of the work of replication: helicase breaks the hydrogen bonds between the paired bases, which unwinds and separates the strands, and DNA polymerase joins the free nucleotides that have paired with the exposed bases of a template strand, building the new strand. The free nucleotides arrive as triphosphates, like ATP, and the energy released when two of their phosphate groups are lost drives the joining.

claims.text: In semi-conservative replication each new DNA molecule holds one whole original strand and one whole newly made strand. Both old strands act as templates, no old strand is split, and the two new molecules are identical to each other and to the original because of complementary base pairing. Conservative means an old strand is kept; semi means only one of the two strands in each new molecule is old.
